# EnterpriseGlue v0.24.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.23.0`.

## Highlights

- **managed engine workload lifecycle:** Adds tenant-bound workload APIs for idempotently registering and decommissioning managed Operaton engines without exposing engine credentials.

## User and administrator impact

- Managed Cloud orchestration can connect and safely decommission a provisioned Operaton engine through a host-owned, dedicated-tenant workload contract.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Cloud control-plane callers must adopt the workload-authenticated registration contract before invoking this endpoint.

## API and integration compatibility

- Adds workload-authenticated registration and decommission endpoints under /api/workloads/tenants/:tenantId with strict requests and signed, credential-free receipts.

## Configuration

- Set EG_MANAGED_ENGINE_INTERNAL_DNS_SUFFIX to the exact managed Kubernetes service suffix; the existing private-host, insecure-HTTP, and engine-host allowlist opt-ins remain required.

## Database migrations

- Implementation reuses existing TypeORM engine, external-registration, authorization, and lifecycle-ledger entities without a schema migration. The focused PostgreSQL persistence lifecycle passed; other supported databases remain a milestone acceptance gate.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Only tenant-lifecycle workload identity may register or decommission a managed engine; browser and general API authentication are rejected, and an absent receipt is signed only when no conflicting engine or registration exists.
- Plaintext credentials are accepted only at the workload boundary for immediate literal AES-GCM encryption and are never returned or logged. Replay identity authenticates the complete request with a domain-separated host-keyed HMAC, not a public password digest.
- Only curated egme-<40 lowercase hex> Kubernetes service URLs under the configured suffix are accepted, and decommissioned engines are denied before outbound transport.

## Documentation

- Updated the engine tenancy/provisioning API, pooled tenancy architecture, and configuration references with the workload lifecycle and endpoint boundary.

## Known limitations

- Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, and Spanner portability remain broader milestone acceptance gates; this change has focused PostgreSQL persistence evidence only.
- A temporary Cloud stop retains the host registration; Cloud observed state must report stopped while host health polling reports the absent runtime unavailable.

## Rollback

- Stop managed Cloud callers from invoking the additive endpoints before rolling back the host. Do not delete provider resources unless a signed host decommission receipt has already been verified; retained engine history remains safe.

## Validation evidence

- Focused unit and contract tests cover schemas, workload authorization, route inventory, idempotency, literal encryption, endpoint policy, runtime decommission denial, and signed absent decommission recovery.
- PostgreSQL integration: 1 test passed for real TypeORM registration, exact replay, encrypted persistence, decommission, credential clearing, signed absence recovery, terminal recreation denial, and concurrent serialization.
- Shared TypeScript no-emit validation passed.
- Pooled-tenancy harness regressions cover bounded CA-verified HTTPS startup, recovery from an interrupted TLS handshake, and fail-closed cleanup. Protected pooled browser qualification remains required.
